justifications.durability: the evidence is a fragment with no regression guard: no test under tests/ or imas_codex/ references the fragment or its anchor, so the 93/15/78 counts can be edited without a gate firing, and the count of array-mentioning chunks is a live-graph value that has already moved from 13 to 12 within the hour under a sibling node's landing. The core negative (getseldata does not name the arrays) is a host fact that is stable, but it too is unguarded. This is the expected durability of an evidence node, not a defect, but it is low.
justifications.evidence: the core claim reproduces independently: I re-ran the host reads through the same wrapper and got hostname intr26-2 (positive control, exit 0), find -type f = 93 files, grep -rniE 'jloop|jtprb|jnprb' exit 1 (0 lines), and the negative-control token eddbreadTime found (33 lines plus binary matches in geteddb.o, libeddbaccess.a, three eddbaccess.ex), so a present token is seen and the zero for the arrays is a real absence. The graph arm reproduces too: I re-ran graph_query.py at the head and got GRAPH_FILE_COUNT=15 with the same 15 paths, and the host-only count 78 and graph-only 0 follow. One drift, benign: the reviewed run recorded 13 CodeChunks mentioning the arrays; my re-run of graph_chunk_tokens.py now returns 12 (18 matching lines vs 19), which the concurrently landed stale-chunk-removal changes ('remove the chunks of code files no longer ingested') explain as graph movement, not a node error. Every value in the fragment's count table is reachable from the cited raw logs.
justifications.fit: the fragment follows the repository's evidence-fragment idiom: a single <section> with a node-prefixed h2 id (getseldata-onhost-grep) and node-prefixed element ids, a compact measure/value table with caption, explicit negative-control and positive-control paragraphs, and a statement of where the arrays actually live. No plan, sprint or ticket label appears in the committed file; it is committed to the section's fragment path and the landing line is in the manifest, not the plan.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's goal was to check on the host whether any getseldata file the scanner missed names JLOOP JTPRB or JNPRB, and to satisfy §14's done-when fallback ('or the run records that the source fills them elsewhere'). The fragment answers it exactly: 0 of 93 host files under /analysis/src/getseldata_v4.2 mention any of the three arrays, the arrays are shown to live in SELENE's routines (SAselene eqadj.f/eqouta.f/mgfild.f/fercor.f/eqvacu.f/nllsqf.f/eqvacu3.f), SAeqread's eqvacu.f and edas2's Eqread.py, all graph-held, so no getseldata file fills them. This is consistent with §14's own statement that JLOOP/JTPRB/JNPRB in SELENE are grid-cell indices, not a channel map.
justifications.reuse: the node adds no product code and duplicates nothing: it reads the graph through the existing GraphClient and the host through the sanctioned ssh wrapper, and its only new artifacts are small read-only probe scripts in the granted reports directory. The fragment reuses the section's existing evidence-fragment shape rather than inventing one.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 4b95b52a8 changes exactly one file, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/getseldata-onhost-grep.html (81 insertions), the one declared in-repo write path; the figure path docs/figures/jt60sa-discovery-completion/getseldata-onhost-grep was granted but correctly left unwritten (the result is a table, and the envelope forbids an image of a table). The run's other outputs live in the granted reports directory outside the repo. No graph write, no code change, no discover run, as the fence required.

negative_control_applied: not required: the reviewed node's write paths reach no test path and its manifest declares 'none'. Its declared host-grep mutation (the token eddbreadTime, present in graph chunks under getseldata) was applied and I reproduced it: eddbreadTime is found in geteddb.c/geteddbt.c and eddbaccess.h:120 on the host, so the procedure sees a known-present token and the zero for the three arrays is a real absence.
